text:
Tyler Seguin is 34 now, playing about 15 minutes a night in a middle-six role for Dallas, and the goals have stopped. He has none in his last ten games and three in 21 overall, on 5.9 expected goals (the quality of his chances, added up). That gap is the whole story: he is shooting 6.1% against a league norm of 13.4%, and our range for his true finishing sits around 12.8%.

Our numbers call him due, not done. Over the ten-game drought he generated 2.7 expected goals on his own shots, a touch above his usual 2.3, and the Stars have scored 5.5 fewer goals than their chances deserved with him on the ice. Pucks like that tend to start falling.

The caveats are real, though. His EDGE skating speed sits in the 13th percentile, and his 5v5 shot share is under water. Evolving-Hockey had him at 0.3 wins above replacement last season, in a small 450-minute sample. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking (six games) liked his passing: 8.0 primary shot assists per 60. Watch whether the shot volume holds; if it does, the points usually follow.
